prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1042; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a side impact at an intersection, with the claimant reporting a neck strain and retaining counsel before any statement was taken.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant's vehicle in the intersection at the time of impact and confirms the claimant was a passenger in that vehicle.

Entry 3: Driver is named on the policy and the policy was in force on the date of loss; nothing in the file suggests the damage predates coverage.

Entry 4: Obtained photos from the scene and statements from two independent witnesses, all of which confirm the collision happened as the claimant and the other driver described.

Entry 5: Inspected the claimant's vehicle. The driver-side door and quarter panel show clear impact damage consistent with a side impact, though a few older scratches elsewhere on the body may predate this loss.

Entry 6: Medical records received show a neck strain diagnosis, and the mechanism and force of the collision appear consistent with that type of injury.

Entry 7: No prior injury to the neck or upper back appears in the records we obtained, and the claimant denies any earlier complaints to that area.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course of physical therapy and medication, with visit frequency tapering as the claimant reported steady improvement.

Entry 9: Counsel forwarded a demand package. Reviewing whether all of the claimed vehicle damage and treatment can be attributed to this impact, as the scope of some repairs is not yet clear.

Entry 10: Claimant provided a follow-up recorded statement adding a few small details about the moments before and after impact; the core account remains the same as the initial report.

Entry 11: Compared the updated statement against the police report, witness accounts and photos, and found the sequence of events consistent across all sources.

Entry 12: Reserve reviewed and file referred for final evaluation of the injury and property components, with the open question on damage scope noted for the handling adjuster.
